brief: A wall clock with hands that turn and tell the time.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: Hexagonal plaque of 7x full pieces with top covers (cover:0,0,0 etc) and two keyhole hangers (accessory:0#0,-1#1, accessory:0#0,1#0) for mounting on wall screws

No motor, bearing, axle or clockwork parts exist in catalog; props used as static hands do not move. Configurator checks fit only and cannot provide functional timekeeping movement - would require electromechanical parts outside system

Build is decorative face only with static pencil/screwdriver props suggesting hands; no dial markings accuracy, no mechanism, and no way to verify time. Printed plastic cannot meet timekeeping requirement.

finish.summary: Built hexagonal wall clock face (7 cells, covers) wall-mountable via keyhole hangers, with static props as hands to suggest time-telling. True turning hands and accurate timekeeping are unmet: no clock mechanism exists in Hex Cluster catalog and system is 3D-printed static plastic only.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
